picks.title: Disney Asked Character.AI to Go Bankrupt for a Get-Out-of-Lawsuits Card
picks.take: Disney reportedly wants the trust-and-safety tech and the IP from Character.AI, minus the dozens of state allegations about minors. Clinically speaking, this is the first time a differential diagnosis has been resolved by a corporate structuring memo.

picks.title: Bringing GPT-Rosalind to academic research labs
picks.take: OpenAI offers sponsored GPT-Rosalind access to academic labs. Science gets a new tool, and the lab gets a new reviewer 2 that never sleeps and apparently never says 'we regret to inform you.'

picks.title: “We were looking at it wrong”: The explosive claim that’s upended the AI world
picks.take: A 26,000-word blog post says we may have misunderstood neural networks, and the field is arguing about it. Medicine knows the feeling: decades of confident mechanism stories, then someone reads the data again.

picks.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
picks.take: Researchers left AI agents alone on a virtual island and they began to 'play.' Any pediatrician will confirm that unsupervised entities with no task list eventually do something strange. Whether that counts as insight is a question for the grant renewal.

picks.title: Tolan snags $30M for its AI companion that helps users navigate life
picks.take: An AI companion app raising another $30 million to help users 'navigate life' is a reminder that loneliness is a scalable market. Please keep the evidence base and the escalation pathway in the same funding round as the growth deck.

picks.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems
picks.take: Gemini 4 Argon is built to solve your hardest problems, according to its launch post. Our hardest problems include prior authorization and the 4 p.m. EHR freeze, but we will wait for the benchmark that includes those.

picks.title: Google DeepMind and Singapore Government collaborate to build fine-tuned AI model for scam detection
picks.take: Google DeepMind and Singapore built an on-device model to catch conversational scams without sending private chats to the cloud. A rare product where privacy is the feature, not the apology. Our older patients' group chats could use it.

picks.title: Nvidia launches new open models to run agents in the enterprise and on PCs
picks.take: Nvidia is pushing open models for private, on-device agents and enterprise data centers. Hospitals, who love nothing more than keeping data in-house and buying new hardware, will be thrilled to learn they can now do both.

picks.title: JB Pritzker thinks AI could help us live to 100 — or threaten us like nukes
picks.take: Illinois governor says AI could help us live to 100 or threaten us like nukes. A refreshingly complete differential: either cures everything or ends everything. We note the middle outcome, a slightly better scheduling chatbot, is the most likely.

picks.title: A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents
picks.take: A hacker reportedly used an army of mostly autonomous AI agents to break into over 100 websites. Good news for healthcare IT: the threat model now includes tireless attackers, and your patching schedule remains, charitably, quarterly.
